author: Sample commentary (synthetic data)
headline: 21 of 111 contractor-affiliated contribution records fall inside a ban window for a covered official; about 40% would by chance.
paragraphs: The contractor contribution ban (§1.126) prohibits contributions from a contractor's principals to officials who approve its contract, from proposal to 12 months after approval. The strip chart places every contractor-affiliated contribution by its days from the nearest contract approval; the shaded band is the window.

Base rate first: contracts and their windows cover a large share of the calendar for active contractors, so some contributions will fall inside windows by coincidence. Here the observed share (31% inside any window) should be read against the 40% expected. Rows tagged 'appears to warrant review' are inside a window and to a covered official; the tag cites the rule and says why, and it is not an assertion that a violation occurred: principals may have been misattributed, contributions may have been returned, and the Ethics Commission may have reviewed the case.

templates.template: {records_fmt} contractor-affiliated contribution records for {contracts_fmt} contracts, {years}: {inside_fmt} inside a window ({inside_share}, vs {expected_share} expected by chance); {covered_fmt} to a covered official (appears to warrant review).
templates.fallback: Too few records match to summarize; widen the years or clear a filter.

caveats.text: Which officials 'approve' a contract depends on the approving body and the contract; the pipeline uses the SFEC-126(f)4 filing's list where available and a rule otherwise (Board of Supervisors for contracts above the Charter threshold, otherwise the department head's appointing officer).
Windows before January 2020 were 6 months after approval, not 12; the pipeline applies the rule in force on the contribution date.
